assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental observation of the Higgs boson in 2012 is a clear, concrete discovery that completed the Standard Model and is exactly the kind of clue from nature I want to see. The 2013 prize recognised the theoretical prediction; the experimental discovery itself has not been honoured.
assessment.attribution: The decisive work was done by the ATLAS and CMS collaborations, each with thousands of members. A fair configuration points to the conceivers and leaders of the two experiments: I propose the ATLAS spokesperson at the time of discovery, the ATLAS founding spokesperson, and a CMS founding leader. The choice among Gianotti, Jenni, Della Negra and Virdee is genuinely contestable.
assessment.maturity: Two independent experiments, with extensive later confirmation of couplings and properties; the interpretation is stable and recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Whether a collaboration-scale discovery can be fairly represented by at most three laureates.
Which of the four credited individuals best represents the decisive contributions; I rely on recollection of leadership roles and have not verified details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube's discovery of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos opened a new window on the universe, with later evidence from the TXS 0506+056 blazar and the Galactic plane. It is a discovery of nature rather than a model, and it matters for our picture of the most violent cosmic accelerators.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led the IceCube concept, Karle was central to the detector and early analysis, and Spiering to the neutrino-telescope tradition from Baikal and AMANDA. The pioneering role of Baikal and AMANDA is a possible credit complication. The collaboration is large, but the leadership is reasonably identifiable.
assessment.maturity: The flux is confirmed by multiple analyses within IceCube and supported by other neutrino telescopes; individual sources are only partly identified, but the existence of the flux is robust.
uncertainties: Whether the origin of the diffuse flux being incompletely understood makes recognition early for some members.
Exact attribution among Halzen, Karle, Spiering and the earlier Baikal and AMANDA founders is uncertain to me.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Inflation explains flatness, horizon uniformity and the origin of primordial fluctuations, and its prediction of a nearly scale-invariant spectrum has been borne out by CMB observations. It is among the most consequential ideas in cosmology, and I know the field well enough to also see its open problems.
assessment.attribution: Guth proposed the idea, Linde the new and chaotic inflation that made it viable, and Mukhanov the quantum origin of structure. Starobinsky is not among the credited names, which weakens the fairness of this configuration and leaves an unresolved allocation of credit.
assessment.maturity: Strongly supported by WMAP and Planck for density perturbations, but the inflaton and a primordial gravitational-wave signal remain unobserved, so confirmation is indirect.
uncertainties: No direct evidence of tensor modes, and alternatives are not fully excluded.
Credit is split across several originators, including Starobinsky who is absent from the supplied names.
Eternal inflation and multiverse concerns bear on how recognition would be perceived.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The first horizon-scale images of M87* and Sgr A* give direct visual evidence of black-hole shadows and are a remarkable achievement in very long baseline interferometry. For someone working on black holes theoretically, empirical constraints near the horizon are very valuable.
assessment.attribution: Falcke proposed imaging the shadow, Doeleman led the EHT effort, and Zensus built VLBI infrastructure and organisation. The EHT involves hundreds of people and many VLBI developers contributed, so the trio is a judgement call.
assessment.maturity: Two independent sources imaged with consistent shadow sizes and follow-up polarisation work; astrophysical interpretation is still evolving but the main result is stable. Recognition is relatively recent but not premature.
uncertainties: Overlap in subject with the 2020 black-hole prize may lower priority.
Attribution within a large collaboration is difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Spectroscopy of exoplanet atmospheres turns exoplanets from detections into physical and chemical worlds and speaks to the question of life elsewhere, which has an existential dimension I find compelling. It follows naturally from the 2019 exoplanet prize and now has JWST data behind it.
assessment.attribution: Charbonneau made the first atmospheric detection, Seager supplied much of the theoretical framework, and Snellen did the first high-resolution ground-based detections; Deming is also a credible early contributor. The allocation among them is not fully clear.
assessment.maturity: Many independent detections with HST, Spitzer, ground-based instruments and JWST; the field is maturing rapidly but interpretations such as molecular abundances still shift.
uncertainties: Possible overlap with the 2019 prize may make the committee reluctant.
Priority questions between early detections and theoretical frameworks.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Planck mapped the CMB with precision that fixed the parameters of the standard cosmological model at the percent level and tightened constraints on inflation; the data remain the reference for cosmology. The enduring value is high, though CMB cosmology has already been recognised through COBE and the 2019 prize.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread over the two instrument teams (LFI and HFI) and the analysis leadership; the named trio is plausible but somewhat arbitrary among many principal investigators, and WMAP covers overlapping ground.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, with results confirmed and extended by ground-based CMB experiments; the findings are stable.
uncertainties: Incremental relative to COBE and WMAP in conceptual terms.
Overlap with the WMAP candidate complicates a fair split of credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Gauge/gravity duality is arguably the deepest theoretical development in high-energy physics of the last thirty years, linking quantum gravity to gauge theories and informing black-hole information, strongly coupled plasmas and condensed matter. I know the subject from my own career and respect its conceptual impact.
assessment.attribution: Maldacena made the conjecture, while Gubser, Klebanov, Polyakov and Witten gave the precise dictionary; Gubser and Klebanov are not among the supplied names, so a fair configuration is incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Enormous internal consistency checks and wide application, but no direct experimental confirmation of the duality as a statement about our universe. Given my wariness of elegant theory not yet tested against nature, I place it below observational discoveries.
uncertainties: Lack of an empirical test in a realistic setting.
Absence of Gubser and Klebanov from the supplied names compromises attribution.
Whether a conjecture satisfies the discovery or invention criterion.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Proposals for quantum computation and simulation with trapped ions and neutral atoms, realised experimentally, laid foundations for quantum technologies; the Cirac-Zoller gate was a key conceptual step and ion experiments realised it.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller made the theoretical proposals and Blatt led the experimental realisation with ions; Bloch is also credited and overlaps with a separate lattice-simulation candidate, so allocation among atom-based approaches is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Mature on the ion side and still developing; the 2012 prize on single quantum systems and the 2025 superconducting-circuit prize partly overlap in territory.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier quantum-systems prizes and with other candidates on this longlist.
The boundary between theoretical proposals and experimental realisations is difficult to draw.
